evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.55, LOWER 'rH' branch off the ring-opened distonic ion, followed down the vertical arrow to the isomerised acyclic diene ion. Book draws 2 arc(s), both single-barbed fishhooks, both starting at an explicitly written H: (i) the H on C5 - the carbon that carries the '.CH2' group - to the radical dot on C4, and (ii) the H on C6 to C5. Net effect of the two drawn hydrogen shifts: the terminal .CH2 becomes the CH3 that the product structure shows, and the radical site walks two carbons along the chain (C4 -> C6), where it ends up adjacent to the allyl-cation carbon C1, i.e. exactly the acyclic 1,3-hexadiene radical cation CH2=CH-CH=CH-CH2-CH3 that the page draws in brackets with '+.'. Moves <2,5> ARE the two drawn fishhooks (each carries one electron of a breaking C-H sigma bond into the forming C-H bond); moves <1,4> (the acceptor radical's odd electron into the forming C-H bond) and <3,6> (the second electron of the breaking C-H sigma bond, left behind on the donor carbon) are implicit hooks required for electron balance and are NOT drawn on the page. LOCALIZATION (convention C): the drawn product carries two fully formed C=C bonds plus a bracketed '+.'; this record writes the localisation in which the second (ionised) pi bond is split into C1(+) and C6(.) on adjacent carbons - the same ion, and the only RDKit-parseable way to place the charge and the odd electron where the mechanism puts them. The migrating hydrogens are isotope-tagged [1H:7] (C5 -> C4) and [1H:8] (C6 -> C5) so RDKit keeps them as separately mapped atoms. 'rH' is the book's random/skeletal hydrogen rearrangement; the prose below the scheme attributes the poor isomeric specificity to 'the tendency of hydrocarbons to undergo random rearrangements'.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.55; no MOD rule variable is cross-linked. The only hydrogen-to-radical-carbon rH encoding in the rule set is hTransition_saturated_2 ('[H]1[C]2[C]3([_A+]4)[C]5[C.]6>>[C.]2[C]3([_A+]4)[C]5[C]6([H]1)', indexed under eq 4.38, comment 'siehe 8.53'), which is a 1,4- (through-space) H shift onto a radical carbon whose 1,3-neighbour carries a charged substituent [_A+]. It cannot match this precursor: its C3 must bear BOTH a charged substituent and a second carbon neighbour with a transferable H, whereas in the distonic ion the carbon adjacent to the charge (C6) has only two heavy neighbours (C1 and C5), both already consumed by the pattern - and the drawn rearrangement here is two consecutive 1,2-shifts, not a 1,4-shift. No MOD rule encodes the 8.55 rH step.

observed_mz 82.0777 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of the rearranged C6H10+. ion (an isomer of the molecular ion, electron-mass corrected). The page prints neither an m/z nor an abundance for it; status 'inferred', no relative_intensity.
